headline: I build AI that survives contact with real systems.
standfirst: I spend most of my time evaluating models, connecting them to real systems, instrumenting the result and making deployments repeatable. My background is in deep learning and computer vision for agriculture, including oil palm and maize disease work in the field. These days I build LLM applications, retrieval systems, developer tools and Linux desktops.

positioning.v: Computer vision · LLM apps · RAG · developer tooling
Available for applied AI and systems roles

roles.note: I worked on deep learning for agricultural computer vision in field conditions and led a research group of five. I co-authored six Scopus-indexed papers, including papers in the Q1 journals Smart Agricultural Technology and Artificial Intelligence in Agriculture.
I mentored 25+ students in Bangkit Academy's machine learning track, from notebook exercises to deployed models. I also reviewed their evaluation plans.
Taught ML, deep learning, data structures and OOP to 200+ students across 14 semesters.

strengths.title: Models meet systems
strengths.body: I connect models to APIs, databases and interfaces, then build the services and data pipelines around them. That can include developer tooling, Linux desktop automation or a cross-platform app. The prototype is often the easy part; I spend my time getting the whole loop to work.

strengths.title: Evaluation as a discipline
strengths.body: I build training and evaluation workflows that carry a project from prototype to deployment. Datasets, experiment tracking and reproducible runs let other people check the result outside the lab.

strengths.title: Field data, honestly
strengths.body: My field work includes oil palm bunch counting in East Kalimantan plantations and computer vision for maize disease under field lighting. The data can be messy, occluded and unlabelled; benchmark scores don't always predict what happens in the field.

strengths.title: Teach what I learn
strengths.body: Teaching ML in the lab and mentoring students taught me to write down my reasoning. If I can't explain a decision to a student, I haven't understood it well enough to ship.

method.body: State the operational question before the model. What decision does this output change?
Get data in and an artifact out with the smallest setup that works.
Choose metrics around the failures the system actually encounters.
Pin the data and build steps so anyone can repeat the run without me in the room.

publicationsNote: Six papers, four published or in review, two under submission. Q1 venues: Smart Agricultural Technology and Artificial Intelligence in Agriculture.

contact.headline: Tell me what you are building.
contact.body: Applied AI, systems work, or a role that combines both? E-mail is fastest. I read every message and reply when there's a clear question.
